set_aside.subject: R0-12 photo binary failure classification
set_aside.text: “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: Which concrete conditions count as a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered: missing bytes, oversize content, an unlisted or unrecognizable media type, an invalid file reference, storage I/O failure, or all of them?
options: Treat missing, oversize, unlisted media, invalid references, and storage I/O failures alike as storage-unavailable
Use storage-unavailable only for missing or inaccessible bytes, with separate failures for oversize and unlisted media
Use storage-unavailable only for infrastructure/storage I/O failures and conceal validation failures
set_aside.default_guess: Treat every post-authorization failure to produce an allowed photo binary, including missing, oversize, unlisted media, invalid reference, and storage I/O failure, as storage-unavailable.

witness.initial: A visible ProgressPhoto record exists and its stored bytes have a media type outside the photo allow-list.
events: An authorized viewer requests that photo.
outcomes: The viewer receives the explicit storage-unavailable error.
The viewer receives a distinct unsupported-media response or the concealed not-found response.

set_aside.subject: R0-12 concealment versus photo storage failure
set_aside.text: “An unknown, cross-project or hidden read is answered the same way … while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: When a photo read is both unknown, cross-project, or hidden and its referenced content is unavailable, which rule takes precedence: the concealed response or the explicit storage-unavailable error?
options: Authorize and check visibility first, so unknown, cross-project, and hidden reads are always concealed without exposing storage state
Return storage-unavailable whenever a resolved photo record has undeliverable content, even if the caller lacks access or the photo is hidden
Define separate precedence for unknown, cross-project, and hidden cases
set_aside.default_guess: Apply authorization and visibility concealment first; return storage-unavailable only for a photo the caller is otherwise authorized to download.

witness.initial: A hidden ProgressPhoto belongs to project A, its stored file is missing, and a viewer has access to project A.
events: The viewer requests the hidden photo by id.
outcomes: The viewer receives the same concealed response as for an unknown photo.
The viewer receives storage-unavailable and thereby learns that the hidden photo record exists.

set_aside.subject: R0-12 storage-unavailable response contract
set_aside.question: What observable HTTP response identifies this error, including its status, JSON error identity, and whether any binary response headers or body bytes may be emitted?
options: Return a defined JSON error with a stable error code and HTTP status before streaming begins
Return an empty response with a defined HTTP status
Allow adapters to choose the status and error representation
set_aside.default_guess: Return a JSON error with a stable storage-unavailable code and a service-unavailable HTTP status, with no binary bytes or download headers emitted.

witness.initial: A visible ProgressPhoto is authorized, but its referenced file is missing.
events: An authorized client requests the photo download.
outcomes: The client receives a JSON error with a stable storage-unavailable code and a defined HTTP status.
The client receives an empty 404, 500, or 503 chosen by the implementing adapter.

set_aside.subject: R0-12 failure after binary delivery starts
set_aside.text: “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: If storage fails after the photo response has begun streaming, is partial delivery permitted, and how is the promised explicit storage-unavailable failure made observable once the HTTP status and headers are committed?
options: Validate or buffer enough before committing the response so every delivery failure can become the explicit error
Permit an aborted partial binary response as the observable storage failure
Exclude mid-stream failures from the storage-unavailable promise
set_aside.default_guess: Do not commit a successful binary response until all checks that can be performed before streaming have passed; if a later read fails, abort the stream and treat the transport failure as storage-unavailable for audit purposes.

witness.initial: A visible authorized photo passes type and size checks, but its storage read fails after some bytes have been sent.
events: An authorized client requests the photo.
The portal sends successful download headers and part of the binary.
outcomes: The client observes only a truncated or aborted binary response.
The portal guarantees an explicit structured storage-unavailable response by avoiding committed partial delivery.
